rated_messages.input_message: Take a slow, deep breath in. And let it out. Now, ask yourself, "Am I willing to go one minute without smoking?" When that minute is over, ask yourself this question again.
Sometimes an urge comes on like a wave. Imagine what it is like to ride the wave as it ebbs and flows. Instead of trying to swim against it, try riding it out until it disappears into the sea.

Add the phrase “I’m having the thought that…” in front of your unhelpful thoughts. For example, “I’m having the thought that I need a cigarette.” Your thoughts are not always true or helpful! They are just thoughts.
No need to get rid of these feelings or control them with a smoke. They are not permanent.
Instead of smoking, think of 3 things from today that you are grateful for. These can be anything, even small things! Now ask yourself, why are you grateful for these things?
Think of your anxious mind like a toddler throwing a tantrum. The best way to respond is to quietly watch, but not give in.
Maybe you could use these few minutes to work out whose birthday is next and what message you'll write in their card? Then when it comes you'll have something original and well thought-out to write!
Stop and take 3 deep breaths. Then decide if you really want to smoke right now or not. Pausing for a few breaths can help lessen the habit.
Setting small goals when you feel unmotivated is best. Maybe a small goal for now is to breathe deeply for the next 3 minutes instead of smoking.
Are you willing to let this urge pass for the sake of living a good long time with the people who matter most to you? When you have an urge, think about the people most important to you.
